reasoning_summary:
Step-by-step verification (blank/markup-only lines carry no claim).
0001 OK: section header recalling Lemma 1; no assertion.
0002 OK: hypothesis T subset of S_3 is admissible.
0004 OK: sup of T exists in the frame L_2, so the notation is well defined.
0007 OK (cited): Lemma 1's conclusion sup T in S_3 is imported as an external lemma and is plausible (T subset of image, choose preimages, phi preserves arbitrary joins).
0009 OK: header for Lemma 2.
0010 OK: hypothesis F a finite subset of S_3.
0012 OK: inf of a finite set exists in L_2.
0015 OK (cited): Lemma 2's conclusion inf F in S_3, imported; plausible by finite-meet preservation.
0017-0020 OK: restatement of the setting.
0022-0025 OK: correct statement of the definition of frame homomorphism (finite meet preserving AND arbitrary join preserving).
0027 OK: header for the join-preservation half.
0029 FAILS: 'Let A subset of S_3' is the wrong ambient set. The very next display forms the supremum sup_1 A in L_1, which requires A subset of S_1; for A subset of S_3 (a subset of S_2) the expression sup_1 A is undefined and phi cannot be applied to it. This is the first step that fails.
0031 OK: no content.
0033 Ill-formed as written (depends on 0029); with the intended A subset of S_1 it is fine, since phi restricted in codomain to S_3 = image of S_1 is a well-defined mapping.
0034-0035 OK: restricting the codomain does not change values, so phi-restricted(x) = phi(x).
0037 FAILS (decisive): the display asserts phi(sup_1 A) = inf_2 phi[A] 'by definition of Frame Homomorphism'. The definition just recalled at 0025 gives arbitrary JOIN preservation, i.e. phi(sup_1 A) = sup_2 phi[A]; nothing licenses turning a join into a meet, and the claim is false in general (e.g. any non-injective phi with |A| > 1 where sup and inf of phi[A] differ). It also contradicts line 0048, which declares the symbols in this section to be suprema.
0040-0041 FAILS: 'inf_2 phi[A] = inf_3 phi[A] by Lemma 1'. Lemma 1 concerns suprema, so it cannot justify a statement about infima; the finite-meet lemma (Lemma 2) is also unavailable since A is arbitrary, not finite. With the intended sup symbols the step would be correct (the L_2-supremum lies in S_3 by Lemma 1, hence is also the supremum for the restricted ordering).
0043-0044 OK in substance (image of A is unchanged by restricting the codomain), but it inherits the wrong meet symbol from 0037/0040.
0046 OK: end of display.
0048 Inconsistent with the display it annotates: it names sup_1, sup_2, sup_3 as suprema, while lines 0037-0043 wrote infima; this confirms the corruption rather than repairing it.
0050 FAILS as a conclusion: arbitrary join preservation does not follow from the chain actually displayed, which ends in a meet in L_3.
0051 Not established: the lemma-level QED is premature.
0053 OK: header for the meet half.
0055 FAILS (same defect as 0029): F should be a finite subset of S_1, not of S_3, since inf_1 F is taken in L_1. ('DefinitiOn' is a harmless typo.)
0057 OK: no content.
0059-0061 OK: phi-restricted(inf_1 F) = phi(inf_1 F) by definition of restriction.
0063-0064 OK: phi(inf_1 F) = inf_2 phi[F] by finite meet preservation, F finite.
0066-0067 OK: by Lemma 2 the L_2-infimum of the finite subset phi[F] of S_3 lies in S_3, and an element of S_3 that is the infimum in L_2 is the infimum for the restricted ordering, so inf_2 phi[F] = inf_3 phi[F].
0069-0070 OK: phi[F] = phi-restricted[F], images agree under codomain restriction.
0072 OK: end of display.
0074 OK: notation consistent with this section's display.
0076 OK: finite meet preservation follows from the chain 0059-0069 (modulo the S_3/S_1 slip at 0055).
0077 OK conditionally: this half is essentially sound.
0079-0080 FAILS: 'The result follows' requires both halves; the join half was not proved.
0082 OK: category tag.
Overall: the meet half is correct, but the join half is broken - it quantifies over the wrong set (0029) and, decisively, replaces the join-preservation identity by a false meet identity attributed to the definition of frame homomorphism (0037), propagating through 0040-0050 and contradicting 0048.
